java-scanner-input-001.title: Read and display a user's age
java-scanner-input-001.instructions: Use `Scanner` to read an integer from `System.in` and display it using the format `Age: <age>`. The automatic tests provide different input values.
hints: Use System.out.println() to display the result.

checks.description: The program reads and displays the age 25.
The program correctly handles another input value.

java.explanation: The tests provide different inputs through System.in and inspect the actual System.out output. This verifies that the program reads values rather than hardcoding one result.

java-animal-class-002.title: Create an Animal class
java-animal-class-002.instructions: Create an `Animal` class with a private `String` attribute named `name`. Implement a public constructor that receives the animal's name and a public `eat()` method that returns the text `'<name> is eating'`.
hints: Declare the name attribute as private.
Use the constructor to initialize the attribute.
Use this.name to refer to the instance attribute.
The eat() method must return a String.

checks.description: The name field exists and has type String.
The class has a constructor accepting a String.
The eat method returns the correct text for a dog.
The eat method also works for another animal name.

java.explanation: The grader uses reflection to verify the compiled class structure, access modifiers, constructor signature and actual method return values. It creates separate Animal objects to test different constructor arguments.
